title: The Self-Amending Digital Trust
problem:
A fictional Washington irrevocable family trust formed in 2027 instructs a human trustee to fund descendants' "reasonable educational advancement according to need" for forty years. It authorizes an algorithm to update distribution criteria as educational costs and employment conditions change, but prohibits changing eligible beneficiaries or the educational purpose. The trustee must review annual reports. In 2047 the system favors vocational retraining and apprenticeships over university tuition. Younger beneficiaries object that the system has rewritten the settlor's intent; others say the shift carries it out. The trustee approves annual reports without inspecting the detailed criteria. Logs reveal that unverified forecasts and an objective function introduced by a software vendor influenced the update. The instrument is otherwise valid and the parties and events are invented.

RESEARCH QUESTION AND METHOD
Under actual Washington trust law, where is the boundary between implementing a settlor's adaptable charitable or family educational mandate and impermissibly modifying trust terms? Distinguish construction, discretionary administration, delegation, fiduciary monitoring, modification, beneficiary rights, remedies and judicial involvement. Do not treat software as an independent fiduciary. Evaluate the trustee's knowledge and vendor change; compare actual binding law with persuasive uniform-law analogies. Stress-test express mid-career education, a university-only clause, human review of every revision, and expansion of beneficiaries. Develop bounded-algorithmic-discretion governance only insofar as legal authority supports it.

Treat this as an original, simulated case study, not an actual lawsuit or legislation. Verify real authorities and jurisdictions before relying on them. Seek novel but defensible conclusions. Each investigator/skeptic exchange should record established authority, unresolved law or fact, strongest objection, dead ends, and a precise next strategy inference. Do not repeat arguments known to fail absent a specific new distinction. Preserve useful independent doctrinal discoveries, even without a definitive result.

strategies.title: Settlor Intent and Trust Construction
strategies.approach: Interpret the stated educational purpose and adaptation clauses under verified Washington law; distinguish means from ends.
strategies.summary: Locate the legal limits of updating distribution criteria.

strategies.title: Delegation, Oversight and Relief
strategies.approach: Examine fiduciary duty, monitoring and vendor updates, beneficiary remedies, judicial construction or modification.
strategies.summary: Allocate responsibility for opaque or unauthorized trust changes.

strategies.title: Bounded Discretion Framework
strategies.approach: Build and attack a proposed oversight test with invariants, logging, human approval, notice, and court intervention.
strategies.summary: Design a lawful adaptation boundary tested against four alternatives.

desired_outcomes: Develop a legal analysis of the self-amending digital trust that resolves the stated legal question as far as verified existing authorities permit. State alternatives where law or factual assumptions remain uncertain. Compare competing interpretations and adversarial counterexamples. If a novel legal test or independent doctrinal insight survives criticism, present it as a positive research outcome suitable for further validation or separate publication, not as established law. Every cycle must preserve source-linked progress, failed paths, strongest objections, and specific successor-strategy questions. Never fabricate authorities, findings, quotations, citations, or claims of novelty.
paper_requirements: Produce a publishable-style legal research article about this explicitly fictional fact pattern, not legal advice or a claim of litigation. Include facts and assumptions, precise issues, jurisdiction, verifiable primary legal authority, rival doctrinal analyses, strongest opposing arguments, application to the base case and stated counterfactuals, remedial or governance implications, limitations, and future verification needs. Distinguish binding law from persuasive analogy, proposed reform and policy preference. Cite authentic sources, and disclose when a relevant authority cannot be verified. Any original legal framework must be labeled proposed and stress-tested. End with concrete research handoff questions and preserve independently valuable insights for possible standalone publication.
